newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank 1996 net profit up 14 percent.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank 1996 net profit up 14 percent.

text.p: Unlisted cooperative bank Rabobank Nederland BA said on Wednesday net profit for 1996 rose 14 percent, based on organic growth both at home and abroad, adding it saw profits rising again in 1997.
It said in a statement with results that growth was expected, partly because of some new activities both in the Netherlands and abroad.
"In line with this, the result will also show continuous growth in 1997, barring unforeseen circumstances," the bank said.
Net profit in 1996 climbed to 1.63 billion guilders ($867.6 million) from 1.43 billion, while operating profit before tax climbed to 2.37 billion guilders from 2.08 billion.
The bank said demand for banking services grew strongly and lending and provision income had seen a double digit rise.

Rabobank said last August its net profit growth was likely to slow to less than 10 percent in H2 of 1996, after it had announced a profit growth of 21.5 percent to 853 million guilders during H1 1996.
The bank also revealed some 3.5 billion guilders of hidden reserves, complying with European Union instructions to publish such reserves, known as VAR funds, by the year 2000.
It shift these reserves into a new open fund, which carries the acronym FAR, and into general reserves.
The new FAR fund is designed for unexpected exceptional loan losses, potential claims and law suits and, under normal circumstances, no deductions will be made from this fund.
Actual loan losses, which were previously covered by additions to the VAR fund, will from 1997 by deducted directly from each banks' profit and loss account.

Analysts expect a one-off rise in bank profits as a result of these changes because they will cut provisions for loan losses, having overprovided for such losses in the past. ($ = 1.878 Dutch Guilders)
